stem: Gastrin stimulates hydrochloric acid secretion primarily from which of the following gastric cell types?

options.label: A
options.text: Parietal cells of the gastric body
options.misconception: None; gastrin drives acid secretion from parietal cells.
options.explanation: Parietal cells produce both hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor, and gastrin is their principal stimulatory hormone, so a gastrinoma drives excess acid production.

options.label: B
options.text: Mucous cells of the pyloric antrum
options.misconception: The antrum is being cast as the acid-producing region.
options.explanation: Cells of the pyloric antrum secrete mucus and hormones, including most of the stomach's gastrin; the antrum is the source of the hormone, not its acid-producing target.

options.label: C
options.text: Chief cells of the gastric fundus
options.misconception: The enzyme-secreting cell is being cast as the acid source.
options.explanation: Chief cells secrete pepsinogen, the inactive precursor of pepsin; they sit beside parietal cells but do not themselves secrete acid in response to gastrin.

options.label: D
options.misconception: A neighboring gland's cells are being cast as gastrin's target.
options.explanation: Pancreatic duct cells secrete bicarbonate-rich juice in response to secretin; they neutralize acid entering the duodenum rather than produce it.

options.label: E
options.misconception: Absorptive cells are being cast as secretory targets of gastrin.
options.explanation: Jejunal enterocytes absorb nutrients across their brush border; they neither secrete acid nor respond to gastrin with acid production.

context: Learning objective: map gastrin to its acid-secreting target. Parietal cells (body/fundus) secrete HCl and intrinsic factor under gastrin stimulation; chief cells secrete pepsinogen; antral G cells secrete gastrin.
imageCaption: Gastric phases cephalic/gastric/intestinal; parietal (HCl+IF), chief (pepsinogen), G cell (gastrin).
